input_text: I have been putting off calling my dad for weeks. Every time I pick up the phone I just find something else to do.
response:
Funny how there's always a dish to wash, isn't there. The dishes have never been so clean as when you're avoiding something.

I don't think you're putting it off because you don't want to talk to him. Usually it's the other way round — it's something you'd only circle this long if it mattered. The ones that don't matter, you make those calls without thinking.

Doesn't have to be a big call. You don't owe him a speech. Just dial it and say you've been meaning to ring. The first ten seconds are the worst of it, and then it's mostly just two people talking.

Is there something in particular making it hard? Or just the general weight of it having gone too long already?

Funny how there's always a dish to wash, isn't there. The dishes have never been so clean as when you're avoiding something.

I don't think you're putting it off because you don't want to talk to him. Usually it's the other way round — it's something you'd only circle this long if it mattered. The ones that don't matter, you make those calls without thinking.

Is there something in particular making it hard? Or just the general weight of it having gone too long already?
